title: How Chaligny taught: snare, counting and keeping time; drumming in the family
summary: Two years of snare drum with a pad, counting aloud and patting the foot; time must come from within the player. He feels drumming was born in him and sees it in his grandsons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Can you tell us a little bit more about your life then, when you started telling us, when we interrupted you about your uncles, when you studied with Mr. Chalier? Okay. Anything else about your lessons? Did you just work on snare drum, or did you have a whole drum set? How did he teach?
Oh, he teached me this with a snare drum.
Oh, by the way, did you have a drum pad any time? Or...
Yeah, when we went to lesson, you used a drum pad at lesson, but when the big band was together, well, everybody had the instruments. They would play the instruments.
Do you remember anything about how he would teach you in counting? If he... Did you count out loud, pat your foot, or any certain way of counting? Oh, yeah, yeah.
You had to count one, two. Slide your foot over. That's right. Yeah. He was very particular about your feet, working with your playing.
Yeah.

Because he said no man can ever play a music unless you use something. Every musician that's played, he got some way to count. Yeah. Some of them will sit and do like that to count. Shake their legs sideways. Yeah, something like that. Some of them, if they're not playing a blowing instrument, they'll hum to themselves. Yeah. You understand? You always, to keep in time, in some ways, about you, you have to keep the time, you know.
Is that what you use, Albert? You use your foot, do you?
The person who's playing a drummer. For a time, well, a drummer, he have to keep his time with the bass drum. That's his time, you see. That's his time. Okay, what do you do with the snare drum?
I mean, when you were learning, did you use your foot with Professor Chaline?
Oh yeah, he made you, yeah. You had to, I mean in counting, that's what you mean. Counting to start off and then you pat your feet. You had to, you see.
How long did you go to Professor Chaline?
I must have went to Chaline about two years. Two years. About two years.
All with the snare drum?

Always with the snare drum, yeah. You see, if you learn music, you wouldn't have to have all the drums. If he would have had orchestra, I would have to bring that out too, you see. But by him, I would have all the class to bring the instrument. It was so many that it would be a brass band. Yeah. You understand? Now, to play an orchestra, I mean you learn music, but the ideas and the feelings would have to come for you to make you be a good drummer. Because they had, many scholars went, didn't make it. As good a teacher as he was. Because if it's not in you.
You can't bring it out if it's not there to start.

But I mostly feel that that was born into me because I loved it. Well, when I got around my uncles and told them what I wanted to do, well they gave me encouragement, you know. And my little grandson reminded me of both of them that if they don't be drummers, I don't know why, because they pick up the sticks and use them they self and they can use, they're not tall enough to reach the small drum when it's on the stand, because I don't have a stand that can come down there, but they'll get on there and they'll stand up and play a good time. I can't even much show you, I'll set them drums up nine. A child is very funny when you want him to do something you won't do it, but they'll get there and they'll play and they should have more attention, but I figure they're quite young, yes, you know, but it's in them because anytime I get the drum they're ready, as ready as I am. Yeah, when we rehearsals here and set the drum up, they'll cry to get on there and play. And I mean, what they're making something, I don't mean that it's beating, it's you can tell it's something in them.
Some real rhythm to it.
Yeah, you understand? Yeah, so I think they will be the same as I was.
Yes, probably will be.
Yeah.
